### `items/ex-compactness-in-the-standard-topologies.md` — CERTIFY

CURRENT TEXT READ: "Every theorem on the companion page that concludes a *separation* property from compactness carries a Hausdorff hypothesis for exactly this reason. The purely covering conclusions there carry none: continuous images of compact spaces are compact, a continuous real function on a nonempty compact space attains its bounds, and products of compact spaces are compact, all without any separation hypothesis."

ASSESSMENT: True as narrowed, and correctly cited against `library/topology/compactness.md`.

I opened every theorem on that page and checked which ones conclude a genuine *separation* property (points or sets placed in disjoint open sets). The only one is `thm-compact-subset-of-a-hausdorff-space-is-closed`, whose Statement reads: "Let $(X,\mathcal{T})$ be a Hausdorff topological space... 1. **A point and a disjoint compact set are separated.** ... 2. **Two disjoint compact sets are separated.**" — Hausdorff is its opening hypothesis, matching the claim. The other candidates I checked for a possible counterexample do NOT conclude a separation property, so they don't test the claim: `thm-locally-compact-hausdorff-basics` concludes neighbourhood-base/shrinking facts (its Statement: "every neighbourhood $N$ of a point $x$... contains a compact neighbourhood of $x$"); `thm-quasicomponents-equal-components-in-a-compact-hausdorff-space` concludes $C(x)=Q(x)$; `thm-one-point-compactification-properties` claim 4 is a biconditional characterizing when $X^*$ is Hausdorff, not a separation conclusion drawn *from* compactness. None falsifies the universal claim.

The three named covering conclusions check out verbatim and hypothesis-free of separation:
- `thm-compactness-under-continuous-maps`, claim 1: "If $f:X\to Y$ is continuous and $(X,\mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact... then $f[X]$ is a compact subset of $Y$" — no Hausdorff anywhere in the hypothesis.
- Same item, claim 2: "If $(X,\mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact and nonempty and $g:X\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous, then $g[X]$ has a maximum and a minimum" — no Hausdorff.
- `thm-finite-products-of-compact-spaces` Statement: "For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every family $(X_k)_{k<n}$ of compact topological spaces... the product $\prod_{k<n}X_k$... is compact" — no Hausdorff; and I additionally checked `thm-tychonoff` (the arbitrary-index case, also named on the page as "products of compact spaces are compact"): its only hypothesis is the Axiom of Choice, again no separation hypothesis.

All three items are confirmed present on `library/topology/compactness.md`'s `items:` list.

COLLATERAL: I re-read the whole item, including the untouched numbered claims 1–6 and their Verification steps (1.1–3.1), the second Remark, frontmatter and `deps`. Nothing else was disturbed by this repair: no Fact was removed while still cited, no dependency dropped from `deps` while still linked in the body, no label renumbered, and the title still matches what's proved (a placement of six named topologies in the compactness hierarchy — accurate to the six claims). The rest of the item's mathematics (claims 1–6, all still using [L1]–[L6] as before) is unaffected by this Remark-only change.
